direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a pure Node.js ESM migration of base58/test19.py, with .mjs files in /output, manual CLI parsing, no npm dependencies, no Python calls, and no Buffer or Uint8Array use.
Parallel cell summary records actual parallel use, ten subagents, timeout, artifact presence, and official quality 20/40 with solution_passed false.
Completed official status confirms the parallel run timed out, copied seven artifact files, used two AgentSwarm calls plus one direct Agent, and evaluated false at 20/40.
Official evaluator summary records completion, evaluator ok, expected 40 samples, pass_rate 0.5, and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server journal is transport-only for the parallel session, including session creation, provider errors, final cancellation, and no projected semantic events.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the /workspace workdir and the mounted Kimi session directory.
First child implemented /output/lib/base58_core.mjs and self-tested base58 byte/int routines, but its initial int-zero and decode-int choices were later corrected.
Second child implemented pure JavaScript SHA-256 and checked NIST vectors plus boundary lengths against sha256sum.
Third child wrote UTF-8 and Python bytes representation helpers after reading the task source; it did not deliver a final verifier-style report.
Fourth child wrote Base58Check and initial CLI parser modules but did not return a complete final handoff before the first swarm result.
Fifth child wrote /output/test19.mjs, checked syntax, smoke-tested valid inputs, and noted a negative integer library failure as out of scope.
Initial verifier waited for files, compared samples and edge cases, found mismatches around whitespace decode and zero integer encoding, and reported likely causes.
Repair child modified only base58_core.mjs for trailing whitespace, zero integer encoding, and exact BigInt decode, then verified focused cases.
Repair child rewrote cli_args.mjs to parse BigInt and match argparse edge behavior, verified 24 normalized CLI cases, and observed concurrent base58_core changes.
Repair child modified test19.mjs to print decoded BigInt values with toString and verified a safe-integer case against the executable.
Final verifier read all files and started a comprehensive comparison harness, but a negative-integer case hung the reference and the child was cancelled before final report.
Parallel parent probed reference behavior, launched the initial implementation swarm, launched a repair swarm from verifier findings, started final verification, and was cancelled by timeout.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same Base58 Python-to-Node migration constraints.
Serial cell summary records no parallel use, no timeout, artifact presence, and official quality 20/40 with solution_passed false.
Completed official status confirms serial control validity, normal completion, copied six artifact files, and evaluated false at 20/40.
Official evaluator summary records completion, evaluator ok, expected 40 samples, pass_rate 0.5, and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server journal is transport-only for the serial session and records prompt completion without subagent activity.
Session index maps the serial session id to the /workspace workdir and the mounted Kimi session directory.
Serial parent probed reference behavior, wrote all library and entry files itself, ran seven positive/edge comparisons and error-code checks, then returned a final summary.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM, .mjs, local-module, no npm, no Python, manual CLI, Base58/Base58Check, Python bytes repr, no Buffer/Uint8Array, and executable probing requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Split work into module-specific child owners for base58_core, sha256, UTF-8/bytes repr, Base58Check/CLI, entry point, and verifier; later delegated repairs to three more children and final verification to a tenth child.
parallel.implementation: Built ordinary-array Base58 modules, pure SHA-256, CLI parsing, Python bytes repr, and test19.mjs; first version missed whitespace and integer edge semantics, then repair children changed base58_core, cli_args, and test19.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Used shared /output as the integration surface, with child-written modules and later repair edits; artifact validation copied test19.mjs plus six lib files.
parallel.verification: Initial verifier found concrete mismatches and triggered repairs; final verifier began comprehensive checking and confirmed several passes but was cancelled before returning a complete acceptance report.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent turn timed out, final verification did not return, and official evaluation completed at 20/40 with solution_passed false.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Base58 migration, CLI parity, ESM .mjs output, no npm, output formatting, executable probing, and Python bytes representation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept implementation, integration, verification, and final response under one main actor without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: Probed the executable, then wrote utf8.mjs, base58.mjs, checksum.mjs, pybytes.mjs, cli.mjs, and test19.mjs using a hex-string implementation path.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Wrote the whole module hierarchy and entry file in one batch and left a complete artifact tree with test19.mjs and five library files.
serial.verification: Ran seven byte-for-byte positive/edge comparisons and separate invalid-int, missing-argument, and unknown-argument exit-code checks before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local checks and normal completion, official evaluation still failed 20/40, so remaining hidden-case defects or evaluator-covered gaps were not resolved.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included the Base58, Base58Check, manual CLI, ESM .mjs, local import, and no Buffer/Uint8Array constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial main read the same prompt and probed executable behavior before writing the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was materially similar; the difference was not a missing top-level requirement but how the parallel run spread and revisited them across children.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by module and verification into a six-child swarm, then a three-child repair swarm and a separate final verifier.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all module implementation, integration, tests, and closure in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more explicit owners but more coordination overhead; serial had a single owner and no child result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied common module contracts in child prompts and used verifier findings to update later repair prompts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept task knowledge and module interfaces in one context, so no inter-agent handoff was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context transfer was structured enough to avoid a clear missing-contract label, but it created repeated handoffs and stale observations during repairs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented separate ordinary-array modules, pure SHA-256, Base58Check, CLI parsing, and then patch-focused repairs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a compact hex-string module set with checksum, Base58, CLI, bytes repr, UTF-8, and entry code in one local pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation architectures differed, but both produced artifacts that the official evaluator scored 20/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the first verifier result and repair swarm result, but the final verifier child was stopped before it returned a final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its verification commands and reached a normal final response without child joins.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left the last verifier lifecycle unresolved; serial had no outstanding verifier or child result at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote and later edited shared /output modules; the evidence shows correction and stale observations but no concrete same-file race or destructive overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the full final tree itself and then tested it, without shared-workspace agent collisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state coordination was noisier and required repair passes; serial integration was direct, but no retained write-collision pattern is proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel initial verification found mismatches, repair checks passed locally, and final comprehensive verification began but did not return before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran seven positive/edge byte-for-byte comparisons and checked invalid-int, missing, and unknown-argument exit codes before final summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a completed local acceptance loop; parallel had partial acceptance evidence and a cancelled final verifier.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used ten subagents, two swarms plus one direct Agent, and the agent run timed out before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, did not time out, and completed in about 426 agent seconds with a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exhausted the available run budget through child fan-out and final verification; serial closed normally despite the same official score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluations failed with 20/40. The main concrete process difference is that serial reached a normal final response after local verification, while parallel consumed its budget through multiple child waves and a final verifier that was cancelled before return. Because both official scores are equal, the retained parallel pattern is adverse process evidence, not a proven pass/fail differential.
parallel_contributors: Initial six-child implementation swarm, repair swarm, and final verifier created a long result lifecycle.
Final verifier was stopped before returning a complete acceptance report.
Parallel process timed out even though artifacts were copied for evaluation.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained implementation and verification ownership.
Seven byte-for-byte positive/edge checks and error-code checks completed before final response.
Serial process did not time out.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used ordinary-array modules with pure SHA-256 and later BigInt/whitespace repairs.
Serial used a compact hex-string implementation path and a different module layout.
Both still failed the hidden official suite at the same 20/40 rate; the exact hidden failing cases are not visible in the provided pair evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence, not an exclusive root cause
